text_blocks.snippet: Common and serious side effects of Jardiance (empagliflozin) range from mild, manageable conditions to rare, life-threatening complications.
snippet_highlighted_words: mild, manageable conditions to rare, life-threatening complications

list.snippet: Urinary tract infections (UTIs): Symptoms include a burning sensation when urinating, frequent urgency, or cloudy/bloody urine.
Genital yeast infections: Vaginal yeast infections in women (itching, thick white discharge, burning) and fungal infections of the skin or penis in men (redness, swelling, pain, or odor).
Increased urination: Going to the bathroom more frequently as the kidneys flush out extra sugar.
Mild effects: Upper respiratory tract infections, increased thirst, nausea, joint pain, or minor weight loss.

Diabetic Ketoacidosis (DKA): A dangerous buildup of acid and ketones in the blood—which can happen even if blood sugar is relatively low. Symptoms include nausea, vomiting, stomach pain, unusual fatigue, fruity-smelling breath, and trouble breathing.

Dehydration: Excessive loss of body water and salt, leading to dizziness, lightheadedness, weakness, or sudden worsening of kidney function (especially if you are older, on a low-salt diet, or taking water pills/diuretics).
Hypoglycemia (Low Blood Sugar): More common if Jardiance is taken alongside other diabetes medications like insulin or sulfonylureas (causes shakiness, confusion, sweating, fast heartbeat).

Necrotizing Fasciitis (Fournier’s Gangrene): A rare, life-threatening bacterial infection of the tissue under the skin in the perineum (area between the anus and genitals) requiring emergency surgery.
Lower Limb Amputations: Increased risk of toe, foot, or leg amputation, particularly in patients with a history of vascular disease or foot ulcers.
Severe Allergic Reactions: Hives, swelling of the face, lips, tongue, or throat, and difficulty breathing.

text_blocks.snippet: More details can be reviewed via the Official Jardiance Safety Guide or the Mayo Clinic Empagliflozin Profile.
